messages.body_plain: Hi there, in a similar situation here. Even though rApache run as a local service manages to pop up an X11 window with the 3d plot on it, any interaction with it is lost, not even resizing-redraw is possible. A suitable solution I've used in the past to share these 3D plots with non-R users was to generate a 3D VRML chunk then rely on an external viewer to open it. I guess it may be possible just to do so then embed that VRML inside your browser page by means of the proper plugin. RGL still produces nicer outputs but with some tweaking VRML can do the job. Hope it helps, Oscar On Jun 20, 7:46 pm, Kajack wrote: > I too have the same question. messages.subject: Re: Having trouble learning how to build frontend with Ext JS
messages.subject_clean: Having trouble learning how to build frontend with Ext JS
messages.body_plain:
You should try with the official documentation. It comes bundled with ExtJS sources, you just need to install Adobe AIR in order to use it. There's a book from Manning: "Ext JS in Action". But I'm not a very big fan of ExtJS, mostly because of it's license (GPL or commercial). I use jQueryUI, which is not as powerful as ExtJS, but is published under GPL and MIT licenses, which allows you to use it for commercial projects. Another reason why I don't like ExtJS are it's size/speed impairments - jQueryUI is lightweight (weights less then 1MB with all the bells and whistles, while ExtJS is about 8MB heavy) and tremendously fast (unlike ExtJS). Though you can't create page elements as easy as you can in ExtJS, it's definitely worth learning. Note the difference between jQuery and jQueryUI! You can check out the tutorial on jQuery on w3schools: http://www.w3schools.com/jquery/default.asp and for jQueryUI, see official documentation: http://jqueryui.com/ .

messages.body_plain:
IMHO, it's not the content-type, it's the brew handler - you're trying to parse an image file with brew() method, and that's what causing the problem. I haven't tested your config, but "RHandler brew" seems a bit odd (shouldn't you put "RHandler brew::brew" instead). And yes, like Jeroen noticed, you also have strange content-type. But is it mandatory to set content-type of an image? I don't think so... Apache deals with that, right? O_o

Anyway... solution: separate img/ folder from the one that contains R scripts. Or use <FilesMatch > directive.

messages.body_plain:
Nice, but note that every single file in /var/www/R/ will be parsed with brew::brew. If you have, say a JS or PHP file alongside R scripts, you will run into errors. <FilesMatch> directive is a beauty, and it's really easy to pass a simple regexp to match files you'd like to parse with brew(). And if you're not writing a spaghetti code (HTML+R with <% %> tags), it's far more useful (and faster) to use base::sys.source

After all... every programmer's problem is just an RT(F)M issue... =)
